name: SHIV SHAKTI POINT — Chandrayaan-3 landing site
blurb: Where Vikram set down in August 2023, on undulating mare-highland regolith south of 69 S. The ground is not steep; it is simply never the same twice.

meta.site: Shiv Shakti Point — Chandrayaan-3 landing site
meta.citation: NASA LRO LOLA polar GDR, south of 60 S, 60 m/px
meta.grid: azimuthal equidistant about the site, resampled bilinear, long axis on bearing 98 deg
meta.resolution_note: source product is 60 m/px; this 1024x512 grid at 4 m/px spans 68 x 34 source posts and is a 15x bilinear resampling of them — interpolation, not added detail
meta.layout: row-major, +x along the traverse, +y to its left
meta.note: Uneven mare-highland regolith; the traverse is over undulating regolith rather than a named grade.

lope.label: LOPE
lope.blurb: The gait the Apollo crews adopted within minutes on every mission. One foot at a time, airborne between every step — a walk whose double support has been replaced by flight.

bound.label: BOUND
bound.blurb: Both feet together, everything into the vertical. The robot is identical on all three bodies and pushes identically, so the whole difference in height and hang is the field.

trip.label: TRIP + RECOVER
trip.blurb: A caught toe, and the fall that follows. Toppling is a pendulum about the toe, so the time to go over scales as 1/sqrt(g): 0.93 s on Earth against 2.28 s on the Moon. That extra second and a third is what the Apollo crews used to get a hand down.
